scenes.headline: "We missed your delivery"
scenes.body: That text may be a scam.
scenes.say: Expecting a parcel? That missed delivery text may be a scam.

scenes.headline: A small fee, a fake site
scenes.body: "Missed delivery" or "address problem", then a look-alike page.
scenes.say: The text claims a missed delivery or an address problem. The link opens a look-alike site that asks for your details, or a small redelivery fee.

scenes.headline: reported lost to text scams
scenes.body: Fake package delivery was the most reported type
scenes.say: In the US, people reported losing four hundred seventy million dollars to text scams in twenty twenty-four. Fake package delivery was the most reported type.

scenes.headline: Then the "bank" calls
scenes.body: A spoofed call says: move your money to a "secure" account.
scenes.say: In the UK, Action Fraud warns the fee can be step one. Days later, a fake bank call tells you to move your money to a secure account.

scenes.headline: The small fee is the bait.
scenes.body: What they really want is your card details.
scenes.say: Analyst note: the small fee is the bait. What they really want is your card details.

scenes.headline: Do this tonight
items: Track it in the carrier's own app
scenes.say: Tonight: don't tap the link. Track the parcel in the carrier's own app or website. And forward the text to seven seven two six, the spam reporting number in the US and UK.

scenes.headline: The security story behind the headline.
scenes.say: Sources are in the description. Follow Securidge.
